mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions 'the difference between the number of X and Y', interpret it as the signed subtraction X − Y, preserving the order of X and Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a phrase 'difference between X and Y' appears to relate counts.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the difference between A and B is 5' as |A − B| = 5 (absolute value) instead of A − B = 5.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements of the form 'A has N more than B' (including 'and C combined') into the equation A − B = N (or A − (B + C) = N), preserving the direction indicated by the wording.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a phrase 'has N more than' linking one person to another (or a sum of persons).
mathgap.example: Reversing the sign and writing B − A = N instead of A − B = N.

mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: Process each 'X gives N Y to Z' statement in the order it appears, immediately subtracting N from X and adding N to Z before handling later statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a transfer statement is encountered.
mathgap.example: Applying all transfers after processing other statements, ignoring their sequential effect.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: Treat each direct count statement 'A has N Y' as setting A's current count at that point, overwriting any previous value.
mathgap.example: Treating a direct count as an immutable initial value and not updating it after earlier transfers.

mathgap.title: Preserve Difference Order
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates a 'has more than' difference to a 'difference between' two other persons, keep the order of subtraction on both sides: (A − B) = (C − D).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering an equality involving differences.
mathgap.example: Swapping the order on one side, interpreting 'A has more than B' as B − A.

mathgap.title: Split Equally Among Recipients
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X splits all the Y they own equally among A and B', set X's count to 0 and give each recipient half of X's original count (allow fractions if needed).
mathgap.example: Giving each recipient the full amount instead of half, or forgetting to zero out X.

mathgap.title: Redistribute Equally Between Two Persons
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'A and B redistribute their Y to ensure each has an equal amount', compute the total of A and B and set each to half of that total.
mathgap.example: Leaving the original counts unchanged instead of averaging them.

mathgap.title: Temporal Evaluation of Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: When processing a relational statement (e.g., 'A has N more than B' or a difference equality), evaluate it using the current counts of the involved persons at that point in the text.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a relational statement is encountered.
mathgap.example: Evaluating relational statements using outdated counts (e.g., initial values) instead of the current counts after prior statements.

mathgap.title: Conditional Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When a statement of the form 'If X has more than N Y, X will transfer their Y to Z' appears, check X's current count; if it exceeds N, move all of X's Y to Z (set X to 0 and add the transferred amount to Z).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a conditional transfer statement.
mathgap.example: Ignoring the condition and always transferring, or transferring only N instead of all of X's count.

mathgap.title: Combined Sum Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'The combined quantity of X, Y, and Z is N' (or similar), interpret it as X + Y + Z = N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a combined quantity statement.
mathgap.example: Treating the combined quantity as a difference or assuming each person has N/3 instead of using the sum.

mathgap.description: Interpreting 'difference between X and Y' as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase 'difference between' is often used colloquially to mean absolute difference, leading the model to drop the sign.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always treat 'difference between X and Y' as X − Y, preserving the order given in the statement.

mathgap.description: Applying all transfers after processing other statements, ignoring their sequential effect.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may batch transfers for convenience, forgetting that later statements depend on earlier updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process each transfer immediately when encountered, updating both parties before moving on.

mathgap.description: Assuming 'A has N more than B' implies A > B and discarding solutions where the computed difference is negative.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The wording 'more than' suggests a positive difference, causing the model to reject negative results.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret the equation A − B = N as a signed relation; the sign of N determines the direction, and A may be less than B if N is negative.

mathgap.description: Treating a direct count statement as an immutable initial value and not updating it after earlier transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may treat direct assignments as fixed base values, ignoring later modifications.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Update the person's count whenever a direct assignment appears, overwriting any previous value.

mathgap.description: Evaluating relational statements using outdated counts (e.g., initial values) instead of the current counts after prior statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may keep a separate snapshot of initial counts and not reflect updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When processing a relational statement, use the latest known counts for all involved persons.
